bureau: Credit Reference Bureau (National Bank of Ethiopia)
note: The National Bank of Ethiopia's Directives for the Establishment and Operation of Credit Reference Bureau, No. CRB/02/2019 (1st amendment), in the bank's own scanned copy (nbe.gov.et, uploaded April 2023; no text layer, read by eye; the bank's media library holds no later CRB directive). The Credit Reference System is run by the Credit Bureau of the National Bank (art. 4.2). Banks update their borrowers' credit information at a minimum once a month (art. 7.4), with no threshold stated: written as reported 30 days after the due date (a monthly cycle). The Bureau retains or displays negative credit information of defaulted loans for a maximum of seven years after the date the defaulted loan is fully settled (art. 6.1.7(b)): the game reads this as a late payment shown while unpaid (keep 30, 'the longest the game keeps') and lifting seven years after it is paid, written as 2557 days (seven years of 365.25 days, as Bosnia and Herzegovina's five years are 1826). The directive's negative information is that of defaulted loans (classified substandard, doubtful or loss, art. 2.9); the form holds one rule for a late payment, so the game applies it to every late payment.

sources.title: National Bank of Ethiopia, Directives for the Establishment and Operation of Credit Reference Bureau, Directives Number CRB/02/2019 (1st amendment) (scanned; read by eye)
sources.said: 4.2. The Credit Reference System shall be operated by the Credit Bureau of the National Bank, which is one of its operational work units. ... 6.1.7. retaining and/or displaying credit information submitted to it for the following set time period; a) positive credit information: - for a minimum of 10 (ten) years after the date of full settlement of the loan and advance. b) negative credit information of defaulted outstanding loans and advances: - for a maximum of 7 (seven) years after the date of full settlement of the defaulted loan and advance. ... 7.4. Financial institutions can update their own credit information on each and every one of their existing borrower provided to the Credit Reference System on an on-going basis; but they shall, at a minimum, update such information once in a month for banks; and once in a quarter for microfinance institutions and capital goods finance companies.
